summary.text: 34-year-old woman with generalized pustular psoriasis first diagnosed in 2018 in her third trimester and confirmed by skin biopsy; she achieved full postpartum remission with systemic corticosteroids, cyclosporine and oral MTX 10 mg weekly for 5 months, then had a mild recurrence in 2020 managed with topical therapy.

In June 2024 she presented with a severe GPP flare with fever and widespread erythematous plaques and pustules; IV hydrocortisone worsened her condition, and MTX 15 mg weekly with daily folic acid was started.

After 3 doses of MTX she developed new annular lip ulcerations and erosions, with hepatotoxicity (ALT 902 U/L, AST 210 U/L), leukopenia, falling hemoglobin and platelets, low albumin and an eGFR of 78 mL/min/1.73 m^(2).

MTX was stopped and she was admitted with suspected toxicity and given IV leucovorin, IV albumin, wound care and supportive measures; serum MTX level was initially unavailable and was undetectable after four days. MRSA grew from a jaw wound culture and nasal swab, IV vancomycin was started, and vitamin B12 deficiency was treated.

On hospital day 4 she developed painful vesicular lesions and punched-out erosions with fever spikes; a Tzanck smear confirmed HSV superinfection, acyclovir led to resolution, and she was discharged on day 9 with ongoing topical therapy.
She was lesion-free at 12 weeks, had a nonfebrile GPP flare at 16 weeks, and a single IV dose of spesolimab led to near-complete resolution of pustules within 24 hours.

evidence.quote: We report a rare case of MTX-induced cutaneous ulceration in a patient with GPP.
